directives.name: The Committee Prevails
directives.title: The Committee Prevails
directives.desc:
Amid a significant amount of political turmoil among Samara's elite, the committee of officers responsible for making all of our statelet's important decisions has decided its successor. Even with Zykov advocating his idealistic "democracy" and General Artsezo promoting the worst kinds of corruption, the committee has thankfully chosen the rational path and nominated Sergey Bunyachenko as the new head of the ROA.

General Bunyachenko is competent and disciplined, perfect for the continuation of the ROA's mission. His first task: to restore stability to our fractured political situation, remind the various officers who really is in charge, and begin shaping the ROA into a force capable of governing.

directives.name: Work with Zykov
directives.title: Work with Zykov
directives.desc:
Although we all accept the leadership of General Vlasov, the ROA has substantial internal factions, each with its own idea of how best to run Samara. General Bunyachenko, for instance, is a fairly standard advocate of a single-party right wing state. Zykov, on the other hand, has far more peculiar opinions. Zykov is an unabashed liberal who campaigns relentlessly for greater democratization. The fact that he had to collaborate with the Third Reich to do so does not seem to faze him.

Although we see eye to eye on very few issues, our faction and his do have the capacity to reconcile. Zykov's supporters, more than anything, desire at least surface-level improvements in the common people's situation. If we can achieve the veneer of progress, we may be able to form a mutually beneficial relationship.

directives.name: Celebrate Vlasov
directives.title: Celebrate Vlasov
directives.desc:
Ah, the great General Vlasov--what an underappreciated man! He defected from the criminal Red Army and brilliantly played the Reich in order to gain the leverage to liberate Samara from the Bolshevik scourge. Now he benevolently leads the ROA, preparing to one day liberate Russia from communism once and for all! Unfortunately, the vast majority of Samara's population does not quite see the situation this way. Most believe him to be a German toady and a traitor to the nation.

If we are to gain any sort of legitimacy, we need to combat the false narratives about our leader and founder. With the help of Zykov and his propagandists, we can tell the Russian people that Vlasov is a hero worthy of respect. In time, they may even believe us.

directives.name: Demote Artsezo
directives.title: Demote Artsezo
directives.desc:
The generals of the ROA are loathed by many Russians as traitors and collaborators, and none more so than Vladimir Artsezo. Artsezo embodies every negative characterization of our organization; he is corrupt, sleazy, greedy, and infamously close to the Germans. Overall, a man of shockingly little moral fiber. He drags Samara down with every day he spends in its senior ranks, but is disconcertingly influential among some less scrupulous officers.

Neutralizing Artsezo as a powerful player in the ROA's politics is a necessity in order to limit the corrosive influence he has on our discipline and popularity. A demotion should do wonders to cut him down to size, as well as showing the skeptical populace that we are capable of dealing with bad actors within our hierarchy.

directives.name: Nominate Zykov
directives.title: Nominate Zykov
directives.desc:
Miletiy Zykov is an impressively principled advocate of democracy. His soaring speeches and firm convictions make him one of our greatest assets in terms of propaganda, performing sorely needed work to rectify the Russian people's perception of the ROA as traitors and assets of the Reich. He is also a snake who should not be trusted with any position of power, lest he steer our army towards his mad dreams of liberalism.

Nevertheless, snakes have their uses. Zykov's way with words makes him the only major politician in Samara with any form of public support. Giving him a prestigious yet powerless sinecure will show the people that we have their best interests in mind, or at least convince them that we do.

directives.name: First Among Equals
directives.title: First Among Equals
directives.desc:
The officers' committee that runs Samara is a democratic institution of ROA generals committed to managing the liberation of Russia. However, as in any organization, certain figures are likely to become disproportionately prominent. General Vlasov, of course, is our most respected leader, owing to his heroism in fighting the Soviets. However, General Bunyachenko has himself rapidly risen in importance following his election by the committee.

To the uneducated masses, this might appear to be evidence that Samara is a military dictatorship, where power is consolidated in the hands of one man. This is naturally a misconception, but one that needs to be corrected to increase trust in our government. Bunyachenko is merely the first among equals, obeyed out of admiration rather than fear. At least, not yet.

directives.name: Sideline the Germans
directives.title: Sideline the Germans
directives.desc:
Out of all the brands and slanderous titles that have been applied to Vlasov and the ROA, none have been more devastating than the accusations that we are German-backed traitors to the motherland. Also quite devastating is the fact that they are entirely true. In order to strike out against the Bolsheviks, General Vlasov made a tactical alliance with the Third Reich. Inconveniently, many German advisors sent over during this period are still present and fairly visible.

The advisors have been far more trouble than they are worth. We have all the weapons we need, and the Reich is not exactly a reliable partner. In the long run, erasing all remnants of our collaboration with Germany will redeem us in the eyes of the Russian people, and our legitimacy as a nation is far more important than our reputation in the eyes of a country that seeks to keep Russia weak and divided.

directives.name: The Committee Looks Outward
directives.title: The Committee Looks Outward
directives.desc: Ever since the Tatars were conquered a long, long time ago, they have been an integral part of the Russian nation. However, with the unfortunate collapse of the country, they believe they have a chance to rise again. We must prove them that this is their greatest mistake. They are our neighbor, and so it shall be easy for the great Russian Liberation Army to march on and crush any hopeless resistance they offer. The time has come for this futile separatist effort to end, and for the Russian flag to fly high over Kazan once again.

He defected from the criminal Red Army and brilliantly played the Reich in order to gain the leverage to liberate Samara from the Bolshevik scourge. Now he benevolently leads the ROA, preparing to one day liberate Russia from communism once and for all! Unfortunately, the vast majority of Samara's population does not quite see the situation this way. Most believe him to be a German toady and a traitor to the nation.

If we are to gain any sort of legitimacy, we need to combat the false narratives about our leader and founder. With the help of Zykov and his propagandists, we can tell the Russian people that Vlasov is a hero worthy of respect. In time, they may even believe us.

SAM_Demote_Maltsev.name: Demote Artsezo
SAM_Demote_Maltsev.title: Demote Artsezo
SAM_Demote_Maltsev.desc:
The generals of the ROA are loathed by many Russians as traitors and collaborators, and none more so than Vladimir Artsezo. Artsezo embodies every negative characterization of our organization; he is corrupt, sleazy, greedy, and infamously close to the Germans. Overall, a man of shockingly little moral fiber. He drags Samara down with every day he spends in its senior ranks, but is disconcertingly influential among some less scrupulous officers.

Neutralizing Artsezo as a powerful player in the ROA's politics is a necessity in order to limit the corrosive influence he has on our discipline and popularity. A demotion should do wonders to cut him down to size, as well as showing the skeptical populace that we are capable of dealing with bad actors within our hierarchy.

SAM_Nominate_Him.name: Nominate Zykov
SAM_Nominate_Him.title: Nominate Zykov
SAM_Nominate_Him.desc:
Miletiy Zykov is an impressively principled advocate of democracy. His soaring speeches and firm convictions make him one of our greatest assets in terms of propaganda, performing sorely needed work to rectify the Russian people's perception of the ROA as traitors and assets of the Reich. He is also a snake who should not be trusted with any position of power, lest he steer our army towards his mad dreams of liberalism.

Nevertheless, snakes have their uses. Zykov's way with words makes him the only major politician in Samara with any form of public support. Giving him a prestigious yet powerless sinecure will show the people that we have their best interests in mind, or at least convince them that we do.

SAM_First_Among_Equals.name: First Among Equals
SAM_First_Among_Equals.title: First Among Equals
SAM_First_Among_Equals.desc:
The officers' committee that runs Samara is a democratic institution of ROA generals committed to managing the liberation of Russia. However, as in any organization, certain figures are likely to become disproportionately prominent. General Vlasov, of course, is our most respected leader, owing to his heroism in fighting the Soviets. However, General Bunyachenko has himself rapidly risen in importance following his election by the committee.

To the uneducated masses, this might appear to be evidence that Samara is a military dictatorship, where power is consolidated in the hands of one man. This is naturally a misconception, but one that needs to be corrected to increase trust in our government. Bunyachenko is merely the first among equals, obeyed out of admiration rather than fear. At least, not yet.

SAM_Sideline_the_Germans.name: Sideline the Germans
SAM_Sideline_the_Germans.title: Sideline the Germans
SAM_Sideline_the_Germans.desc:
Out of all the brands and slanderous titles that have been applied to Vlasov and the ROA, none have been more devastating than the accusations that we are German-backed traitors to the motherland. Also quite devastating is the fact that they are entirely true. In order to strike out against the Bolsheviks, General Vlasov made a tactical alliance with the Third Reich. Inconveniently, many German advisors sent over during this period are still present and fairly visible.

The advisors have been far more trouble than they are worth. We have all the weapons we need, and the Reich is not exactly a reliable partner. In the long run, erasing all remnants of our collaboration with Germany will redeem us in the eyes of the Russian people, and our legitimacy as a nation is far more important than our reputation in the eyes of a country that seeks to keep Russia weak and divided.

SAM_The_Committee_Looks_Outward.name: The Committee Looks Outward
SAM_The_Committee_Looks_Outward.title: The Committee Looks Outward
SAM_The_Committee_Looks_Outward.desc: Ever since the Tatars were conquered a long, long time ago, they have been an integral part of the Russian nation. However, with the unfortunate collapse of the country, they believe they have a chance to rise again. We must prove them that this is their greatest mistake. They are our neighbor, and so it shall be easy for the great Russian Liberation Army to march on and crush any hopeless resistance they offer. The time has come for this futile separatist effort to end, and for the Russian flag to fly high over Kazan once again.
